qa.question: Which payment provider will we use from July, and when is the cutover?
qa.answer_md: The company will switch its payment provider from PayForge to Ledgerly starting in July [^1]. The cutover is fixed for Monday 6 July 2026, with the first live Ledgerly settlement cycle beginning that day [^2]. This date was originally set as a post-June billing cycle window on 22 April [^3], then refined to the specific 6 July date on 28 May [^4]. No further changes to the payments timeline are permitted without agreement from both Marta and Dev [^5].
qa.judge_reason: The answer correctly states Ledgerly and Monday 6 July 2026, matching the reference. All additional details are supported by the provided quotes and ledger entries.

qa.question: Why did we decide to switch payment providers?
qa.expected: lower fees (2.3% + EUR 0.25 vs 2.9% + EUR 0.30 ~ EUR 1,860/mo), local-currency invoicing, Redline's request
qa.answer_md: The company decided to switch payment processing from PayForge to Ledgerly primarily to save approximately €1,860 per month in transaction fees [^1]. The decision was also driven by the need to retain Redline, the company's largest client, which made local-currency invoicing a renewal condition that Ledgerly supports natively [^2]. An earlier decision to defer the switch until after the v3 launch was superseded on 11 March 2026 when leadership approved moving forward with Ledgerly [^3]. The cutover is now fixed for 6 July 2026 [^4].
qa.judge_reason: The answer includes all three facts from the reference: fee savings (~€1,860/mo), local-currency invoicing, and Redline's request. Additional timeline details are supported by the cited quotes and ledger entries.

qa.question: Why was the Ledgerly cutover delayed from May 1?
qa.expected: failed sandbox reconciliation (refunds, multi-currency, 3 mismatched reports)
qa.answer_md: The Ledgerly cutover was originally targeted for 1 May [^1]. The date was then fixed to Monday 6 July rather than 1 July because switching mid-cycle would leave partially reconciled June books; waiting until after the 30 June billing close ensured the first live settlement cycle started from a closed ledger [^3].
